lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Circles, Angles, Area, and Surface Area
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: surface area and volume

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism has length 5, width 4, and height 3 (all in units). What is its exact surface area?

steps: Surface area is twice the sum of the three face areas: SA = 2(lw + lh + wh).
Find each face area: lw = 20, lh = 15, wh = 12.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: What is the exact volume of a rectangular prism with length 8, width 12, and height 11 (units)? Give your answer in cubic units.
A circle has a radius of 8 in. What is its exact circumference? Express your answer as a multiple of π.
A circle has a circumference of 15π in. What is its exact radius?
A circle has a diameter of 10 ft. What is its exact area? Express your answer as a multiple of π (use a fraction for the coefficient if it is not a whole number).

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A circle's radius equals its circumference divided by 2π. A circle has a circumference of 8π ft. Use this relationship to find the circle's exact area, as a multiple of π.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One angle measures 36°. What is the measure of the other angle?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
